mainTopic: Whether יום כיפור atones for violating itself, and how ישראל and כהנים get their יום כיפור atonement according to רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון
overview: The גמרא first tries to prove that רבי agrees that יום כיפור does not atone for breaking יום כיפור itself, since otherwise daytime כרת could never happen. The proof is pushed away: a person could choke and die, or eat just before sunset, leaving the day no time to atone. Next, the משנה seems to call ישראל, כהנים and the כהן משוח both equal and different. רב יהודה explains that all of them are atoned by the שעיר המשתלח for ordinary sins, while the פר atones for the כהנים for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. A ברייתא shows that this is רבי יהודה's view. רבי שמעון disagrees and holds that the כהנים get all their atonement from the פר, learning this from a היקש between the two goats. רבי יהודה reads that היקש as only requiring the goats to match in look, height and price. Finally, the גמרא asks who taught a ברייתא sending the כהנים to פרו של אהרן. רבא says רבי שמעון, while אביי shows that it can fit רבי יהודה too; אביי's explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Without a limit, there would be no daytime כרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a proof that רבי must agree יום כיפור does not atone for breaking יום כיפור itself, because otherwise daytime כרת could never happen.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי, there would be no case of כרת for eating on the day of יום כיפור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof. It argues that רבי must agree that the day of יום כיפור does not atone for someone who breaks יום כיפור itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that the day of יום כיפור atones even without תשובה. If it also atoned for breaking the day itself, then anyone who ate during the day would be forgiven by the rest of that same day. Then the תורה's punishment of כרת for eating on יום כיפור would never apply, so רבי must agree there is an exception.

keyTerms.meaning: Spiritual 'cutting off,' the תורה's punishment for eating on יום כיפור
Daytime
There is none / he does not have it

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying רבי rejects כרת. It is saying that רבי's view would leave no room for כרת, which is why he must agree to an exception.

phrases.english: Karet for the daytime
phrases.notes: He means כרת for eating or working during the day of יום כיפור.

phrases.english: according to Rabbi, there would be none.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof from the previous section about רבי's view of how יום כיפור atones.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי agrees the day of יום כיפור does not atone for violating יום כיפור itself
steps.raayaSupportSource: The logical need for the תורה's כרת for eating on יום כיפור to be possible

steps.title: Daytime כרת can still happen: death or eating near sunset
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof by giving two cases where the day had no time left to atone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not? You can find daytime כרת if he ate a piece of meat, choked on it, and died. Or he could have eaten right before sunset, so there was no time left in the day to atone for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from step 1. It shows that כרת for eating during the day is still possible even if the day atones for breaking itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The day can only atone if some of it is still left after the sin. If the person died right away, or the day ended right after he ate, the atonement never had a chance to take effect. So רבי's view does not cancel the תורה's כרת, and the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Why not?
You can find it (a case where it happens)
A piece of meat
Sunset
Time, enough time

steps.whatToRemember: The proof about רבי is rejected. Even if the day atones for breaking itself, כרת can still happen when there is no time left for the day to atone.

phrases.english: Why not?
You can find it
where he ate a piece of meat, and it choked him and he died;
or alternatively, where he ate
close to sunset,
so there was no time
to atone for him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 1 by showing that daytime כרת can still happen.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof that רבי must agree the day does not atone for breaking itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the day can always atone, but it cannot atone when the person dies or the day ends right after the sin.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: ישראל, כהנים, and כהן משוח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה that groups ישראל, כהנים, and the כהן משוח together.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: Both ישראל, and כהנים, and the anointed כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This is a setup line: it prepares for the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists three groups: ordinary Jews, regular כהנים, and the כהן גדול. The word אחד ('both / equally') suggests that all three are treated the same when it comes to atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: Both... and... (meaning they are treated equally)
The anointed כהן, meaning the כהן גדול
Ordinary Jews who are not כהנים

phrases.english: Both Israelites and priests
and the anointed priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאֶחָד כֹּהֲנִים וְאֶחָד כֹּהֵן מָשׁוּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of רבי and moves on to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישראל, כהנים, and the כהן משוח are listed together as equal in atonement.

steps.title: The משנה seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the משנה can call the three groups equal and then ask what the difference between them is.
steps.simpleTranslation: This משנה is difficult by itself. It teaches that ישראל, כהנים, and the anointed כהן are all the same. Then it teaches: what is the difference between ישראל, כהנים, and the anointed כהן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out an inner contradiction in the משנה. First it says the three groups are equal, and then it says there is a difference between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אחד means they are the same, while מה בין means they are different. Both cannot be true unless they refer to different kinds of atonement, and that is what the next step will explain.

keyTerms.meaning: This itself is difficult (the text contradicts itself)
It teaches
And then it teaches
What is the difference between

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
It teaches: Both Israelites and priests
and the anointed priest;
and then it teaches:
What is the difference between Israelites
and priests and the anointed priest!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in step 3 by comparing it with the next line of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה first calls the groups equal (אחד) and then says they differ (מה בין), which looks like a contradiction.

steps.title: רב יהודה: equal for ordinary sins, different for טומאת מקדש
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that the groups are equal in being atoned by the שעיר המשתלח for other sins. They differ only in that the פר atones for the כהנים for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that this is what the משנה means: ישראל, כהנים, and the anointed כהן are all atoned by the שעיר המשתלח for other sins, and there is no difference between them. So what is the difference between them? Only that the פר atones for the כהנים for making the מקדש or its קדשים טמא, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the contradiction by splitting the משנה into two topics. The groups are equal for one kind of sin and different for another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ordinary sins, everyone is atoned the same way, through the שעיר המשתלח. For the special sin of טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, the כהנים are atoned through the פר of the כהן גדול instead of through the goats. So 'equal' and 'different' are both true, because each one refers to a different kind of sin.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means
The goat sent away to עזאזל on יום כיפור
Other sins
The bull the כהן גדול brings on יום כיפור
Entering the מקדש or eating קדשים while טמא

steps.whatToRemember: All three groups are atoned by the שעיר המשתלח for ordinary sins. Only for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו do the כהנים get atonement through the פר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא solves a contradiction: each part of the text is talking about a different situation.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: This is what it is saying:
Both Israelites and priests
and the anointed priest
achieve atonement through the scapegoat
for other transgressions,
and there is no distinction between them.
And what is the difference between Israelites
and priests and the anointed priest?
Only that the bull atones for the priests
for defiling the Temple and its sacrificial foods, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each half of the משנה refers to a different kind of sin
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say the groups are both completely equal and also different in the same matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are equal for other sins through the שעיר המשתלח, and different only for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, where the פר atones for the כהנים.

steps.title: The author of the משנה is רבי יהודה, proven from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה follows רבי יהודה. It brings a ברייתא that reads ויקרא 16:33 word by word to list everything and everyone atoned for on יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is the משנה? It is רבי יהודה's. A ברייתא teaches: 'He shall atone for the holy sanctum' means the קודש הקדשים. 'The Tent of Meeting' means the היכל. 'The altar' means just what it says. 'He shall atone' means the courtyards. 'The priests' means just what it says. 'The people of the congregation' means ישראל. 'He shall atone' means the לויים.
steps.whatsHappening: Having explained the משנה (all groups share the שעיר המשתלח), the גמרא now names its author as רבי יהודה and starts quoting a ברייתא to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first maps each phrase of the פסוק to a place or a group. The word 'יכפר' appears twice in the פסוק, and each time it is read as adding something new: first the courtyards, then the לויים. This list sets up רבי יהודה's ruling in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And who is it? A question asking who the author of a teaching is
The innermost place, the קודש הקדשים
The Sanctuary, the room outside the קודש הקדשים
The courtyards of the בית המקדש
Just as it sounds, its plain meaning

phrases.english: And whose view is it? It is רבי יהודה, as it was taught in a ברייתא:
phrases.notes: 'It' is the משנה as רב יהודה just explained it.

phrases.aramaic: ״וְכִפֶּר אֶת מִקְדַּשׁ הַקֹּדֶשׁ״ – זֶה לִפְנַי וְלִפְנִים;
phrases.english: 'He shall atone for the holy sanctum': this is the innermost place;
'the Tent of Meeting': this is the Sanctuary;
'the altar': as it sounds;
'he shall atone': these are the courtyards;
'the priests': as it sounds;
'the people of the congregation': these are the Israelites;
'he shall atone': these are the Levites;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the author of the משנה as explained by רב יהודה in step 5
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה follows רבי יהודה

steps.title: רבי יהודה: everyone shares one atonement
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that all the groups are equal: they are all atoned for by the שעיר המשתלח for other sins. This is רבי יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: All of them are made equal in one atonement: they are atoned for by the שעיר המשתלח for other sins. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי יהודה's ruling, which matches the משנה exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק lists כהנים, ישראל and לויים together, רבי יהודה says one offering, the שעיר המשתלח, covers all of them for other sins. This matches the משנה's 'אחד ישראל ואחד כהנים' as רב יהודה explained it in step 5, which shows that the משנה is רבי יהודה's.

keyTerms.meaning: They were made equal
One atonement shared by all
Other sins, meaning sins besides טומאת מקדש וקדשיו

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, the שעיר המשתלח atones for everyone, כהנים included, for other sins. Only for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו do the כהנים have their own פר.

phrases.english: All of them were made equal for one atonement,
in that they are atoned for by the scapegoat
for other sins.
These are the words of רבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reading of the פסוק with רבי יהודה's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שעיר המשתלח atones for ישראל, כהנים and לויים alike for other sins

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the כהנים have a separate atonement
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the כהנים are atoned for by the פר, and not by the goats. This applies both to טומאת מקדש וקדשיו (through its blood) and to other sins (through its confession).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: Just as the blood of the goat done inside atones for ישראל for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, so the blood of the פר atones for the כהנים for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. And just as the confession over the שעיר המשתלח atones for ישראל for other sins, so the confession over the פר atones for the כהנים for other sins.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי שמעון, who disagrees with רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון sets up two exact parallels. The goat's blood matches the פר's blood, and the שעיר המשתלח's confession matches the פר's confession. So the כהנים never rely on the שעיר המשתלח at all. That means the משנה, which has the כהנים atoned for by the שעיר המשתלח, cannot be רבי שמעון's.

keyTerms.meaning: The inner goat, whose blood is brought inside the Sanctuary
The blood of the כהן גדול's bull
Confession said over the animal
Entering the מקדש or eating holy food while טמא

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two goats. The inner goat's blood atones for טומאה, while the שעיר המשתלח (sent away) atones for other sins through its confession.

phrases.english: רבי שמעון says:
Just as the blood of the goat that is done inside

phrases.aramaic: מְכַפֵּר עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל טוּמְאַת מִקְדָּשׁ וְקָדָשָׁיו,
phrases.english: atones for Israelites for defiling the Temple and its holy foods,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ דַּם הַפָּר מְכַפֵּר עַל הַכֹּהֲנִים
phrases.english: so too the blood of the bull atones for the priests
for defiling the Temple and its holy foods.
And just as the confession over the scapegoat
atones for Israelites for other sins,
so too the confession over the bull
atones for the priests for other sins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view within the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פר atones for the כהנים for both טומאת מקדש וקדשיו and other sins; the goats atone only for ישראל

steps.title: But the פסוק puts everyone together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון: the פסוק clearly lists כהנים and ישראל together, so they must be equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי שמעון, they were certainly made equal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי שמעון can separate the כהנים, when the פסוק groups them together with everyone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names כהנים and 'עם הקהל' in one breath, and רבי יהודה used this to say they share one atonement. That seems hard to deny, so the challenge is how רבי שמעון reads the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: But certainly, a strong 'surely this is so'

phrases.english: And according to רבי שמעון,
surely they were made equal!
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק itself puts the כהנים and ישראל side by side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי שמעון's view using the פסוק from the ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's separation of the כהנים' atonement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק lists all groups together, which implies one shared atonement

steps.title: Equal in needing atonement, but each gets its own
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי שמעון, the groups are equal only in that all of them receive atonement on יום כיפור. Each group is atoned for through its own offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'made equal' mean? That they are all people who get atonement. But each one is atoned for by its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי שמעון by narrowing what the 'equality' in the פסוק means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק joins the groups only to teach that all of them get atonement on יום כיפור. It does not teach that they share the same offering, so the כהנים can still use their own פר. This removes the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: People who receive atonement
However, but
By its own, separately

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה says the groups share one atonement. רבי שמעון says they are equal only in getting atoned for, and each group gets its own atonement.

phrases.english: What does 'made equal' mean?
That they are all subject to atonement;

phrases.aramaic: מִיהוּ כֹּל חַד וְחַד מְכַפַּר בִּדְנַפְשֵׁיהּ.
phrases.english: however, each and every one is atoned for by its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge to רבי שמעון
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the scope of the equality
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק's grouping means one shared atonement
steps.terutzMaskana: The grouping means only that all of them receive atonement; the means of atonement differ

steps.title: What is the source for רבי שמעון's view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind רבי שמעון's view that the goats do not atone for the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון holds that the כהנים get no atonement from the goats. This question sets up the next step, where the גמרא gives his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 8, רבי שמעון said the כהנים are atoned for only by the פר. The פסוק lists everyone together, so we need to know what source tells him that the שעיר המשתלח does not cover the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: What is his reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?
phrases.notes: His view from Step 8: the כהנים are atoned for by the פר, not by the goats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבי שמעון against the challenge from the פסוק, the גמרא now asks for his positive source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for excluding the כהנים from the atonement of the שעיר המשתלח.

steps.title: The two goats are linked, so neither atones for the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'he shall take the two goats' links the שעיר המשתלח to the inside goat. The inside goat does not atone for the כהנים, so the שעיר המשתלח does not either.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says: 'He shall take the two goats.' This links the שעיר המשתלח to the goat brought inside. The inside goat does not atone for the כהנים for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, because the פסוק says about it 'of the people.' So too, the שעיר המשתלח does not atone for the כהנים for other sins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון learns from a היקש, a link between the two goats made by one פסוק. Whatever is true of one goat is true of the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inside goat clearly excludes the כהנים, because the תורה calls it the goat 'of the people.' Since the תורה joins the two goats together, the same rule carries over to the שעיר המשתלח. That is why the כהנים get no atonement from it for other sins either.

keyTerms.meaning: It was linked (by a היקש) so that the same rules apply to both
The goat whose blood is sprinkled inside the קודש הקדשים
'Of the people', meaning the ordinary Jews and not the כהנים
Other sins, not connected to טומאה in the מקדש

phrases.english: As it is written: "And he shall take the two goats"
the goat that is sent away is linked
to the goat that is offered inside.
Just as the goat offered inside
does not atone for the priests
for impurity of the Temple and its holy foods,
since it is written about it: "which is for the people";
so too, the goat that is sent away

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ מְכַפֵּר עַל הַכֹּהֲנִים בִּשְׁאָר עֲבֵירוֹת.
phrases.english: does not atone for the priests for other sins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A היקש between the two goats carries over the exclusion of the כהנים from the inside goat (taught by 'אשר לעם') to the שעיר המשתלח.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the link only means the goats must match
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the link between the goats only teaches that they must look alike, be the same height, and cost the same. It says nothing about whom they atone for.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה would tell you: the goats were linked for this purpose only, to teach that they must be equal in appearance, in height, and in price.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי יהודה deals with רבי שמעון's source. He agrees there is a link, but he says it teaches something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides accept the היקש. They disagree about what it teaches. For רבי יהודה it only sets physical rules for choosing the two goats, so the שעיר המשתלח can still atone for the כהנים for other sins.

keyTerms.meaning: For this purpose
Appearance, height, price

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה does not deny that the two goats are linked. He only limits the link to how the goats look and what they cost, not to whom they atone for.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda would say to you:
for this they were linked:
that they should be equal in appearance, in height, and in price;
that is what it comes to teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how רבי יהודה reads the same היקש that רבי שמעון relies on in Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source: the היקש teaches physical equality, not equality in atonement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The היקש makes the goats equal in everything, including whom they atone for.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יהודה, the היקש only requires the goats to match in appearance, height, and price.

steps.title: Which תנא taught that the כהנים are atoned for by אהרן's bull?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who taught a ברייתא saying the inside goat does not atone for the כהנים, and that they are atoned for through the bull of אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who taught what the רבנן taught in a ברייתא: 'He shall slaughter the goat of the חטאת which is for the people.' This teaches that the כהנים are not atoned for through it. Then through what are they atoned for? Through the bull of אהרן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא and asks which opinion it follows. This step sets up the question; the rest of the ברייתא comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from 'אשר לעם' that the inside goat does not cover the כהנים, and it says they are covered by פרו של אהרן instead. This sounds like רבי שמעון's view in Step 8, so the גמרא wants to know who the author is.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא who taught this?
The bull of אהרן, the כהן גדול's own bull on יום כיפור

phrases.english: Who is the one who taught that which the Rabbis taught:
"And he shall slaughter the goat of the sin-offering which is for the people":
that the priests are not atoned for through it.
And through what are they atoned for?
Through the bull of Aaron.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the dispute over the היקש to identifying the author of a related ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא is the author of the ברייתא that sends the כהנים to פרו של אהרן for atonement.

steps.title: The ברייתא proves the כהנים do get atonement
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא considers that the bull might not help the כהנים, since it is called 'his own'. It then proves from 'he shall atone for the כהנים' that they do have atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think the כהנים are not atoned for through the bull of אהרן either, since it already says 'which is his own.' Would they then have no atonement at all? When it says 'he shall atone for the כהנים,' we see that they do have atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. It raises a possible doubt about the bull and then answers it from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אשר לו' could suggest the bull is only for אהרן himself. That would leave the כהנים with no atonement at all. The פסוק 'יכפר על הכהנים' shows the כהנים must have some atonement. The next step decides whether it comes from the bull or the inside goat.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought
'Which is his own', said about אהרן's bull
If so, from now on
We have found

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא has shown only that the כהנים must have some atonement. Which offering provides it is decided in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לֹא יִתְכַּפְּרוּ בְּפָרוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן;
phrases.english: One might think they are not atoned for through the bull of Aaron;
for it has already been said: "which is his own".
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:6. 'His own' sounds like the bull is only for אהרן himself.

phrases.english: If so, do they have no atonement at all?
When it says: "he shall atone for the priests",
we have found that they do have atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יִתְכַּפְּרוּ בְּפָרוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in Step 14, proving that the כהנים do have some atonement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Although the bull is called 'אשר לו', the פסוק 'יכפר על הכהנים' shows the כהנים must have some atonement.

steps.title: The bull of אהרן fits better than the inside goat
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks which offering atones for the כהנים. It answers that the bull of אהרן fits better, because the bull already reaches beyond אהרן himself to cover his household. The inside goat never stretches like that.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what gives them atonement? It makes more sense that they get it from אהרן's bull. That bull already goes past its basic rule, because it also covers his household. It makes less sense that they get it from the goat done inside, because that goat never goes past its rule to cover his household.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is still speaking. It now explains why the כהנים are atoned through אהרן's bull and not through the inside goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15 the ברייתא proved that the כהנים do have some atonement. Now it picks between the two offerings. The bull is called 'his own', yet it already covers his household too, so stretching it a bit further to cover all the כהנים is reasonable. The goat belongs to the people and is never stretched to include אהרן's house.

keyTerms.meaning: they receive atonement
it is better / it makes more sense
the bull of אהרן (the כהן גדול's own יום כיפור bull)
it was released from its general rule (an exception was made)
the goat whose blood is brought inside the קודש הקדשים

phrases.english: Through what do they get atonement?
It is better that they get atonement through the bull of Aaron,
since it was already released from its basic rule regarding his household,
phrases.notes: The bull is called 'his own,' yet it also covers his household, so it already reaches past אהרן alone.

phrases.english: and let them not get atonement through the goat that is done inside,
since it was not released from its basic rule regarding his household.
phrases.notes: The inside goat is for the people. We never see it stretched to cover אהרן's household.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמָּה הֵן מִתְכַּפְּרִין? מוּטָב שֶׁיִּתְכַּפְּרוּ בְּפָרוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 15. Having shown that the כהנים have atonement, it now decides which offering provides it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים are atoned through the bull of אהרן, which already reaches beyond אהרן to his household, and not through the inside goat.

steps.title: A second proof from a פסוק in תהלים
steps.stepSummary: In case the reasoning can be challenged, the ברייתא brings a פסוק. It calls all the כהנים 'בית אהרן', so 'his house' in the bull's פסוק can include every כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want to argue with that reasoning, the פסוק says: 'House of אהרן, bless the Lord; house of לוי, bless the Lord; those who fear the Lord, bless the Lord.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a backup proof from a פסוק, so the point does not rest on reasoning alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bull atones for אהרן 'and his house.' The פסוק in תהלים uses 'בית אהרן' for the whole group of כהנים, next to 'בית הלוי' for the לויים. So 'his house' can mean all the כהנים, and the bull covers them.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you want to say otherwise (introduces a backup proof)
the house of אהרן, meaning all the כהנים
the house of לוי, meaning the לויים

phrases.english: And if you wish to say otherwise,
look, the verse says:
"House of Aaron, bless the Lord;
house of Levi, bless the Lord;
those who fear the Lord, bless the Lord."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם נַפְשְׁךָ לוֹמַר – הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a backup proof from a פסוק for the conclusion reached by reasoning in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That 'his house' in the bull's פסוק includes all the כהנים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 135:19–20, which calls the whole group of כהנים 'בית אהרן'.
steps.whatToRemember: According to this ברייתא, the כהנים are atoned through אהרן's bull, because 'his house' means all the כהנים.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: the ברייתא does not follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again who taught the ברייתא. רבי ירמיה says it cannot be רבי יהודה, because he holds that the כהנים do get atonement from the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who taught this? רבי ירמיה said: not רבי יהודה. If it were רבי יהודה, he says that כהנים do get atonement through the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא comes back to its question from step 14 about who taught the ברייתא. רבי ירמיה first rules out רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא implies that without the bull, the כהנים would have no atonement at all. But רבי יהודה (step 7) holds that the שעיר המשתלח atones for the כהנים too. So according to him they would never be left with nothing, and the ברייתא cannot be his.

keyTerms.meaning: who is the תנא who taught this?
the goat sent away to עזאזל (the scapegoat)

phrases.english: Who taught it?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה;
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said: It is not like Rabbi Yehuda,
for if it were Rabbi Yehuda, doesn't he say:
"Priests have atonement through the scapegoat"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תַּנָּא? אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the ברייתא has been fully quoted, this returns to the question from step 14 about who taught it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view the ברייתא follows.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not רבי יהודה, since he holds that the כהנים are atoned through the שעיר המשתלח.

steps.title: רבא: the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, who holds that the כהנים get no atonement from the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.simpleTranslation: So whose view is it? רבא said: it is רבי שמעון, who says that כהנים do not get atonement through the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא names who did teach the ברייתא. רבא says it is רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון (steps 11–12), the goats do not atone for the כהנים at all. So if the bull did not cover them, they really would have nothing. That is exactly the worry in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: so whose view is it?

phrases.english: So whose view is it?
Rava said: It is Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: ״כֹּהֲנִים אֵין לָהֶם כַּפָּרָה בְּשָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ״.
phrases.english: who says: "Priests have no atonement through the scapegoat."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַנִּי? רָבָא אָמַר: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי יהודה is ruled out, this names the positive answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון, who denies that the כהנים get atonement from the שעיר המשתלח.

steps.title: אביי: the ברייתא can still fit רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the ברייתא can follow רבי יהודה. Its worry is only about atonement for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, which the scapegoat does not cover. The כהנים have atonement for other sins, so they must have it for this sin too.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: you can even say it is רבי יהודה. This is what the ברייתא means: if so, would they have no atonement for making the מקדש or its holy foods impure? When the פסוק says 'he shall atone for the כהנים,' we see that they have atonement for other sins. And just as they have atonement for other sins, so too they have atonement...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי disagrees with רבי ירמיה and רבא. He rereads the ברייתא so that it fits רבי יהודה after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the scapegoat covers the כהנים for other sins. But טומאת מקדש וקדשיו is covered only by the bull or the inside goat. So the ברייתא's question, 'otherwise they have nothing,' is only about that one sin. Since the פסוק shows the כהנים have atonement for other sins, they must also have it for this one.

keyTerms.meaning: you can even say
entering the מקדש or eating holy food while impure
other sins

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the scapegoat fails to help the כהנים. For רבי יהודה it does help, but only for other sins. The ברייתא's question is limited to טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Abaye said: You can even say it is Rabbi Yehuda,
and this is what it is saying:
If so, would they have no atonement
for impurity of the Temple and its holy foods?
When it says: "He shall atone for the priests,"

phrases.aramaic: מָצִינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן כַּפָּרָה בִּשְׁאָר עֲבֵירוֹת;
phrases.english: we find that they have atonement for other sins;

phrases.aramaic: וּכְמוֹ דְּמָצִינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן כַּפָּרָה בִּשְׁאָר עֲבֵירוֹת,
phrases.english: and just as we find that they have atonement for other sins,
so too they have atonement

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on רבי ירמיה and רבא by rereading the ברייתא so that it fits רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the ברייתא: it is only about one kind of sin.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means the כהנים have no atonement at all without the bull, which contradicts רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means only that they would lack atonement for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. Under רבי יהודה the scapegoat still covers their other sins.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that one ברייתא can fit two different תנאים, depending on how narrowly you read its question.
